ranking.note: Raised to P1: fixing flaky-by-design relay-delay timeouts is the category's stated top concern (red CI hides real failures), and it closes a long-standing issue #19732.
Raised to P1: brings previously unfuzzed BIP157 p2p message handlers under fuzzing and already surfaced a real net_processing integer overflow (#36321).
Raised to P2 for consistency with #36327: both are measured, broad test-runtime wins (7-15 min per fuzz CI job) that every contributor pays for.
Moved up: a lint job that silently passes while compilation fails is a misleading CI signal, which this category ranks near the top.
Moved up: hidden Qt unit-test output on Windows CI means failures cannot be diagnosed at all, a signal problem rather than mere polish.
Moved up: TSan adaptive delay plus centralized sanitizer defaults improves race-detection signal across all runners, more than a config cleanup.
Moved up: invariant checking in debug CI jobs is active defect detection, comparable to the other sanitizer/CI signal PRs grouped here.
Moved up: unblocks running several local CI containers at once (#35416), a concrete developer workflow blocker rather than a nicety.
Moved up: fixes a benchmark that silently measured the wrong thing (verbosity 3 identical to verbosity 2), i.e. a misleading-signal fix.
Moved down: benchmark-realism improvement with an overlapping, larger-scope alternative to #36254; value is real but clearly deferrable.
Moved down slightly to sit with the other profiling-tooling benchmarks, below signal and framework work.
Moved down: a single wallet benchmark serving one optimization PR (#27865) ranks below framework and CI-signal work in this category.
Moved down: coverage of a small REST helper is narrower than the p2p/consensus coverage items placed above it.
Moved down: mostly test-code deduplication with a fidelity improvement; no current failure or coverage gap of high-risk code.
Moved down: author states no test fails today; purely preventative harness hardening.
Moved up within P4: it does remove real compiler warnings and adds enforcing linters, making it the strongest of the mechanical cleanups.
Lowered to P4: reviewers judge fuzzing wallet RPCs without chain/UTXO context to have very low efficacy, so the coverage claim is weakly justified.
Lowered to P4: author prefers abandoning the automated check in favour of manual rewrites, leaving the stated payoff speculative.
Moved down: the variable is set by no in-tree CI job and the PR is NACKed as unused, so there is no demonstrated problem in this repo.

inconsistencies: #36254 and #32554 solve the same benchmark-fixture problem from opposite ends (#36254 adds undo data for the existing block413567 fixture; #32554 deletes that fixture in favour of a generator, superseding #32457). Review #36254 first as the minimal correctness fix, then decide whether #32554's generator replaces it.

Three PRs touch unit-test assertion machinery and will collide: #35713 (in-tree runner with BOOST_* shims), #35139 (new ASSERT/ASSERT_EQ macros shareable with fuzz), and #36091 (operator<< for tested types, explicitly preparing types for #35713). The direction decision in #35713 should be taken first; #36091 is largely a prerequisite for it and #35139 duplicates part of its assertion story.

#34969 and #36068 both rework wallet fuzz harness setup (FuzzedWallet construction/reuse) for throughput; they overlap textually and should be reviewed as a pair, #36068 first since it changes the wallet lifetime the other optimizes within.
#35442 depends on #35433 (deprecating the replaceable RPC arguments) and currently bundles its commits while in draft; it cannot land before that chain element.

#31349 (failing CI on non-loopback traffic and DNS queries) and #35417 (assigning per-container dynamic IPv4/IPv6 subnets) both change CI container networking assumptions; merging one without the other in mind risks false failures. #35417 defines the addresses that #31349 must tolerate.
#36074 and #36087 are both mechanical util/check.h sweeps over the same test files by the same author; #36074 should go first to avoid a second rebase of a hundreds-of-files diff.
#32409 duplicates nothing but is dead code in this tree: no in-tree job uses MSVC debug builds or sets the variable, and it carries an explicit NACK on that ground.
result.notes: No P1s were assigned by the per-PR passes; I created two, because the category's own ordering puts flaky/misleading-test signal first and unfuzzed p2p message handling second, and #36306 and #36337 are the clearest instances (the latter already produced a real net_processing bug report). The middle of the list was re-sorted around one axis: PRs that restore or protect a trustworthy CI signal (#36235, #36024, #36308, #35957, #36254, #36129) were lifted above pure coverage-and-benchmark additions (#34360, #35827, #35964, #32554), which the individual assessments had ranked partly by novelty. Band boundaries otherwise stand: the twelve original P4s plus #35342 and #35994 are all narrow, cosmetic, or weakly justified within test infrastructure.
